newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault plant hit by truckers' strike.
newsitem.headline: Renault plant hit by truckers' strike.

text.p: French carmaker Renault SA has set short-time working for 24 hours at its Sandouville plant beginning on Tuesday afternoon because of a truckers' strike that has blocked parts deliveries, plant managers said.
The plant produces Safrane, Laguna and Laguna Nevada car models.
Renault on Monday halted production at its Douai plant, which was blocked by truckers demanding that the government pressure their employers on wages and retirement benefits.
A company spokesman said the group was examining the situation at its other plants and would shortly announce its plans for the week.
Officials at the PSA group's Peugeot and Citroen divisions said they expected to announce any plans for short-time working at their plants in early afternoon.
The Peugeot car division last week set short-time working at its Sochaux and Poissy plants in France and at its Madrid plant and Ryton plant in the U.K.

Officials said previously scheduled plans for short-time working, reflecting weak car demand in France, had been moved forward at several plants. A Citroen spokesman said short-time working set for Friday at the Rennes plant was brought forward to Monday.
